name: Malicious Link

evidence.rationale: Even when a user clicks a malicious link, DNS filtering can prevent successful navigation when the destination domain is known to be malicious.

9.3 helps prevent link-based and web-based initial access by stopping users from reaching malicious or unapproved content in the first place. It does this by requiring updated network-based URL filtering across all enterprise assets, using methods such as category-based filtering, reputation-based filtering, and block lists. In practice, this means enforcing controls that restrict access to unsafe websites, malicious downloads, risky scripts, and unauthorized browser extensions, reducing the risk of phishing, exploitation, and malware delivery. If 9.3 is implemented as a secure web gateway or proxy that can stop the post-click fetch/download, then this technique is applicable.
Network intrusion prevention solutions can block requests to malicious links and prevent associated content from being downloaded across monitored network boundaries.
Web proxies and application-layer gateways can block requests to malicious links and prevent associated content from being downloaded.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
